dimension_justifications.soundness: The schedule/NFE arithmetic, boundary cardinalities, half-step median discussion, and distinction between bootstrap stability and false-positive control are internally consistent. However, the central empirical object cannot be interpreted or rebuilt without the event-time coordinate, recorder schema, inclusion rules, events, programs, and result vectors. All empirical quantities are explicitly source-reported/cannot-verify, while the selector lacks a calibrated arm-level null and the strongest probes are marginal or single-locus.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is unusually candid, well structured, anonymous, within the nine-page main-text limit, and explicit about its composite intervention, evidence strata, post-treatment amendment, missing vectors, and non-mechanistic scope. Evaluation is nevertheless obstructed by absent probe vectors, unavailable event semantics, and repeated presentation of unauditable source-reported values.
dimension_justifications.contribution: Separating algebraic boundary-set reachability from event-dependent magnitude is a useful reporting principle, and the non-nested probes are directionally informative. The scientific contribution remains narrow: one private checkpoint, one task, one active recorder, a jointly varied partition/allocation schedule, reused development evidence, and no experiment identifying recorder, sampler, model, or allocation mechanisms.

paper_summary: The paper studies positionwise identity-lock time in blockwise diffusion-language-model decoding under an active-block recorder. It varies block length while fixing model family, questions, canvas for the main arms, total NFE, decoding rule, and temperature, and reports that a finite-grid min–max selector follows the configured block length for L16/L64 main arms, a reused L32 development control, and sequential L24/L48 probes. It supplements this with same-profile rank-sum ordering, bootstrap stability summaries, a narrow spectral residual probe, and a separate content-association analysis. The paper ultimately advances a scoped measurement recommendation rather than a mechanism claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verifiable contribution is the formal and presentational separation between a priori boundary-set composition and conclusions requiring observed magnitudes. The printed NFE sums, candidate-boundary cardinalities, event-row multiplication, GPU-hour conversion, and claim that even-sample integer observations permit half-integral medians are internally correct. The empirical selector outcomes themselves remain source-reported and cannot be independently verified from the snapshot.
strengths: The design strata are disclosed rather than pooled rhetorically: reused development control, two main arms, sequential probes, and the separate content bed are identified as materially different evidence tiers.
The manuscript correctly states that bootstrap mode fractions and zero observed misses measure resampling stability, not false-positive rates or coverage.
The composite partition-plus-required-allocation treatment and absence of mechanism identification are explicitly acknowledged.
The L24 marginal conditional margin, L48 single boundary locus, L32 control band touching zero, post-treatment scope amendment, and missing probe vectors are reported prominently.
The candidate-set counts and NFE arithmetic are consistent: the displayed schedules each total 48 NFE, and the reported boundary/interior cardinalities follow the finite difference domains.
The paper includes anonymity, reproducibility limitations, and an AI-assisted preparation disclosure.
questions: What is the exact semantic type and origin of each step label in Ti,r: global function-evaluation index, block-local index, or position-observation ordinal? How are these coordinates made comparable across blocks and schedules?

For every arm and position, how many decode-position pairs are absent, censored, terminal, or otherwise excluded from Ar, and do P* and sep(P) persist on a common complete-case set and under explicit censoring alternatives?
Can the complete six-candidate separation and rank-sum vectors, candidate tie rules, replicate indicators, and exact question-pairing manifest for L24/L48 be supplied?

What portions of the estimator, candidate grid, null construction, probe sequence, and decision scope were fixed before each data tier, and can timestamped registration records and diffs substantiate that chronology?

How is the rank-sum score normalized across candidates with very different boundary-set sizes, how are ties and dependence among adjacent differences handled, and why should its ordering be stable under a cluster-aware calibration?

Would identical decoded trajectories retain the reported periodicity under a passive full-canvas recorder, and can partition and per-block allocation be varied separately enough to identify which component places or scales the boundary?
Why is BIN8 foregrounded in the setup while BIN16 becomes the load-bearing content null, and was the granularity ladder and interpretation fixed before observing the result?

issues.location: PDF p.3, Section 2, Eq. (1), paragraphs “Identity-lock time and finite observation domain,” especially the discussion following Eq. (1); PDF p.8, Section 4, “Event semantics” limitation; PDF pp.15–16, Appendix B
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that it cannot determine whether step labels are global, block-local, or position-observation ordinals and lacks rules for empty observation sets, absent final values, censoring, and terminal/unresolved positions. Ar is therefore an unavailable source-defined set that may vary with r. This is a demonstrated specification omission; whether it actually biased the reported profiles cannot be verified.
issues.why_it_matters: The central estimand compares medians and adjacent differences across positions and schedules. Coordinate resets, block offsets, or outcome-dependent inclusion can mechanically create, erase, or rescale boundary jumps. Without these semantics, the meaning of a d-unit and comparability of m(r) across blocks are unresolved, so the headline periodicity could be an observation/encoding artifact.
issues.required_fix: Provide the complete event-schema and recorder contract, executable lock-time construction, coordinate conversion, final-value rule, and arm-by-position accounting for missing, censored, terminal, and excluded cases. Report sensitivity analyses using a common complete-case population and explicit alternative censoring/terminal encodings.
issues.verification_test: An independent rebuild from the supplied events must reproduce every m(r), d(r), sep(P), P*, boundary locus, and bootstrap indicator. Recompute the candidate ordering under each plausible time-coordinate and missingness convention; the central conclusion must remain unchanged or be narrowed to the conventions under which it holds.
issues.evidence_needed: Reviewer-safe event streams or sufficient deterministic aggregates, schema documentation, implementation, inclusion masks, per-position denominators, and sensitivity outputs.

issues.location: PDF p.2, Section 2, “Numerical provenance”; PDF pp.5–7, Tables 2–6 and Figure 2; PDF pp.12–13, Table 9; PDF pp.15–16, Appendix B; reviewer-safe repository inventory and experiment registry
issues.observed_evidence: Every empirical value is labeled source-reported/cannot-verify. Events, analysis programs, machine-readable results, registration records, pairing manifests, replicate indicators, figure data, and complete probe/rank-sum vectors are absent. The manifest hashes are internally consistent, but they authenticate only the incomplete frozen package. No numerical discrepancy is demonstrated; the numerical claims simply cannot be independently checked.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper’s contribution is empirical, yet no headline estimate, uncertainty result, probe argmax, registration chronology, or sensitivity statistic can be recomputed. In particular, the reported probe choices and rank-sum candidate orderings cannot be established from the printed partial cells.
issues.required_fix: Release a reviewer-safe evidence supplement containing machine-readable arm profiles and full candidate vectors, analysis code, configurations, replicate-level outputs or deterministic seeds, pairing metadata, registration records, and figure-generation inputs. A private checkpoint may remain restricted if the derived evidence and complete provenance are independently auditable.
issues.verification_test: Run the supplied pipeline in a clean environment and require exact or tolerance-specified agreement with Tables 2–14 and Figure 2, including all omitted probe candidates, rank-sum orderings, bootstrap modes, positivity indicators, permutation counts, and chronology hashes.
issues.evidence_needed: Complete reviewer-safe numerical bundle, executable analysis, configuration files, full output digests, and timestamped registration artifacts.

issues.location: PDF pp.3–4, Section 2, “Matched intervention and scope”; PDF p.8, Section 4, “Composite intervention” and “Recorder and control arms”; PDF p.9, Conclusion
issues.observed_evidence: Changing block length changes both partition boundaries and ordered per-block step allocation, while the active recorder itself exposes only the current block. No uniform-allocation/factorial arm or paired active-versus-passive recorder is run. This confounding is demonstrated by the design and correctly acknowledged by the paper.
issues.why_it_matters: P*=L under this intervention cannot identify whether the boundary pattern arises from recorder visibility, block-state transfer, per-block allocation, or model behavior. The result is therefore an association with a composite schedule and cannot validate a mechanism or establish that the active recorder caused the apparent periodicity.
issues.required_fix: Either retain a strictly descriptive case-study claim throughout or add mechanism-discriminating controls: record identical trajectories through active and full-canvas/passive instruments, vary allocation separately from partition where feasible, and include a clean negative or null schedule.
issues.verification_test: A preregistered factorial or matched-recorder analysis should estimate recorder, partition, and allocation contrasts separately. A mechanism claim is supported only if the predicted contrast changes occur while non-target components are controlled and clean controls remain silent.
issues.evidence_needed: Dual-recorder paired trajectories, allocation/partition control arms, preregistered contrast definitions, and uncertainty for component-specific effects.

issues.location: PDF pp.3–5, Sections 2 and 3.1; PDF pp.5–7, Tables 2–5; PDF p.8, Section 3.2 and Limitations; PDF pp.12–13, Tables 8–9
issues.observed_evidence: The L32 arm is a reused development control involved in estimator development; L16/L64 are the two main arms; L24/L48 are sequential, separately registered, different-canvas probes. The model-intrinsic branch was withdrawn after main-treatment data. L24 has pmargin=0.071, L48 has only one selected boundary locus, and the L32 positivity fraction is 0.8805. These limitations are disclosed, but registration timestamps and complete probe vectors cannot be verified.
issues.why_it_matters: The five rows are not independent or equally confirmatory. Development reuse can favor the estimator, sequential probe choices permit adaptation, the canvas change alters the observation domain, and a one-locus L48 result provides no across-boundary replication. Consequently, the evidence does not support a uniform five-confirmation reading or robust generalization.
issues.required_fix: Run a genuinely held-out, preregistered confirmation set with full candidate reporting, unchanged analysis, multiple boundary loci per selected period, and a fresh in-session L32 control. Preserve explicit stratification and report sequential decisions and multiplicity.
issues.verification_test: Before opening outcomes, freeze grids, schedules, scope, and stopping rules. Confirm P*=L and the required criterion on the held-out arms, with at least several boundary loci and complete vectors; verify that conclusions do not depend on the reused control or L48’s single locus.
issues.evidence_needed: Timestamped preregistration, fresh control, longer or replicated non-power-of-two probes, full candidate vectors, and independent held-out results.

issues.location: PDF pp.3–5, Section 2, paragraphs on selection stability, median discreteness, and rank-sum; PDF p.5, Table 2; PDF p.7, Table 5; PDF pp.12–13, Appendix A.5–A.6 and Table 10
issues.observed_evidence: Bootstrap mode and positivity fractions measure resampling stability, not selector false-positive probability. The original permutation gate flags 10/25 wrong candidates. The corrected margin remains an unadjusted, construction-specific conditional or cross-condition diagnostic rather than full-selector calibration. The rank-sum “z” values lack complete candidate scores, tie correction, dependence treatment, normalization details, and inferential calibration, and reuse the same profiles. These facts are mostly acknowledged, so no false significance result is demonstrated; the inferential support is absent.
issues.why_it_matters: The selector can be stable under resampling yet systematically choose schedule-induced structure under a clean null. Candidate boundary sizes range from 1 to 31 and adjacent differences are dependent, so uncalibrated standardized rank-sums are not comparable or inferential by default. The alternative ordering therefore supplies limited robustness evidence.
issues.required_fix: Calibrate the complete selection pipeline under structure-preserving clean/null arms, report family-wise false-selection rates and power across plausible effect shapes, and fully specify a cluster-aware rank-sum statistic with tie handling. Otherwise remove standardized “z” terminology and retain only an explicitly descriptive ordering.
issues.verification_test: On simulated and empirical known-clean arms, the frozen selector and alternative statistic should attain the stated family-wise error target; on preregistered positive controls they should show adequate power. Full candidate rankings must reproduce under cluster-aware permutations or bootstrap resampling.
issues.evidence_needed: Null-generating protocol, clean controls, full candidate score vectors, dependence-aware resampling code, empirical type-I error and power curves, and tie/normalization specifications.

issues.location: PDF pp.13–15, Appendix A.7–A.8, Eq. (3), Tables 11–12; PDF p.8, “Content scope” limitation
issues.observed_evidence: The supporting content analysis excludes terminal-resolved units, retains 6,178 of 6,274 candidate units, has a median resolved-pair fraction of 0.575, and is measured only on the separate L32/NFE32 bed. Its result survives through BIN16 but becomes zero-power at BIN32. The setup foregrounds BIN8 while the appendix calls BIN16 load-bearing. Events and code are unavailable, so bias from outcome-dependent resolution cannot be assessed.
issues.why_it_matters: Excluding units or pairs based on resolution can select on the lock-time outcome and alter the confidence association. The conclusion is also conditional on null granularity and cannot support cross-length or mechanism interpretation.
issues.required_fix: Report exclusions by cause and arm, define zero-pair and terminal handling, provide bounds or sensitivity analyses for excluded/censored units, explain the preregistered status of BIN8/BIN16, and keep the finding explicitly separate unless replicated on L16/L64.
issues.verification_test: Recompute the association under plausible terminal/censoring encodings, common-support restrictions, and preregistered non-degenerate null granularities. The stated content conclusion should persist without selecting a favorable granularity post hoc.
issues.evidence_needed: Unit-level inclusion masks, exclusion reasons, complete null ladder outputs, preregistration, and missingness/censoring sensitivity results.

ethics_concerns: No human-subject, privacy, or deployment-risk issue is apparent from the frozen snapshot. The missing model/prompt record for the inherited AI-generated qualitative figure is a provenance/documentation concern rather than a material research-ethics concern, and the figure is labeled non-evidentiary.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by a fresh, isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. It used only the frozen submission snapshot and did not access the internet, prior reviews, repository history, author notes, or files outside the snapshot for substantive paper evidence.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A complete reviewer-safe event and analysis bundle that independently reproduces all profiles, candidate vectors, resampling summaries, figures, and registration chronology.
An explicit event-time and missingness contract, with robustness of P*=L across common-case and plausible censoring/coordinate conventions.
Fresh preregistered held-out controls and non-power-of-two probes with multiple boundary loci, complete candidate reporting, and no dependence on the reused L32 development arm.
A paired active-versus-passive/full-canvas recorder experiment and allocation/partition controls that identify which component generates the boundary pattern.
Full-selector structure-preserving null calibration, empirical false-selection rates, power analyses, and a fully specified cluster-aware rank-sum sensitivity analysis.
Replication across additional checkpoints, tasks, schedules, canvases, and recorder implementations if broader significance is claimed.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to reproduce any printed candidate separation, bootstrap fraction, probe argmax, rank-sum ordering, or spectral/content result from released artifacts.
Evidence that the selected period changes under a reasonable global-versus-local time-coordinate convention or missing/terminal encoding.
Timestamped records showing that candidate grids, probes, null granularities, or decision scope were chosen after inspecting the corresponding outcomes without being labeled exploratory.
A clean dual-recorder or null-schedule control that exhibits the same selector behavior, indicating that the claimed diagnostic distinction has no specificity.
Complete L24/L48 vectors showing an undisclosed tie, alternative argmax, or sensitivity to the smallest-period tie rule.
Material question mismatch in the claimed paired bootstrap or unhandled dependence that invalidates its joint summaries.
review_limitations: The snapshot intentionally omits raw events, executable analysis, private checkpoint, complete probe vectors, and registration artifacts, so empirical truth and chronology could not be independently verified.

The bibliography-wide citation audit is explicitly incomplete, and internet access was prohibited; contribution and novelty judgments therefore rely only on the supplied citation lock and manuscript positioning.
The PDF was inspected in full through its rendered text/layout extraction; the raster Figure 2 could not be regenerated or numerically inspected because its source data and generator are absent.
